newsitem.title: USA: Fla Gov vetoes $35.8 mln of projects, signs budget.
newsitem.headline: Fla Gov vetoes $35.8 mln of projects, signs budget.

text.p: Florida Gov. Lawton Chiles signed the state's $42.2 billion budget into law after vetoing $35.8 million of projects late Wednesday.

The fiscal 1998 budget contains no new taxes, but raises tuition by 7.8 percent for state university undergraduates, 8.7 percent for graduate students and 12.8 percent for out-of-state students at public universities.
It increases public school spending by $696.6 million and social services spending by $207.4 million. Spending for public safety rose by $81.3 million, including $69 million for prison construction.

The biggest item Chiles vetoed was a $12 million appropriation to build residential academies in Dade and Duval counties to help students at risk of dropping out of public schools. He said he supported the idea, but that the veto was necessary because legislation authorizing the academies was never enacted.
He also killed a $2.8 million allocation for beach renourishment projects because the money would have been drawn from the Hurricane Catastrophe Fund.
Chiles' line-item vetoes have varied during his years in office, reaching $106 milion in 1991 and dipping to $8 million in 1994.
